organization: ASD ACSC, CISA, NSA, CCCS, NCSC-NZ, NCSC-UK
title: Careful adoption of agentic AI services
scope: Agent privileges, identity, trust boundaries, autonomy, oversight, supply chain and accountable operation.
limitations: ASD publication date; NSA announced it on April 30. Recommendations require system-specific implementation and evidence; this is not an executable benchmark.

title: NSA announcement: Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services
scope: Confirms NSA participation, publication timing and joint authorship of agentic AI guidance.
limitations: Announcement supports provenance; use the complete joint guidance for substantive control interpretation.

title: CISA and Partners Release Guidance on Adopting Agentic AI Services
scope: Confirms CISA participation and recommendations to bound autonomy and strengthen identity and oversight.
limitations: Official bulletin hosted by GovDelivery. This is a release notice, not a separately scored framework.

title: Agentic AI harnesses: The layer above the model
scope: Security responsibilities of orchestration, context, tool execution, memory, permissions and operational controls.
limitations: ASD publication; do not attribute joint authorship to NSA or CISA. A secure model alone does not establish harness security.

organization: NSA, CISA and international partners; ASD host
title: Deploying AI Systems Securely: Best Practices for Deploying Secure and Resilient AI Systems
scope: Infrastructure hardening, deployment controls, data protection, monitoring and secure AI operation.
limitations: ASD page date. Focuses on operating externally developed AI, especially on-premises or private cloud; adapt infrastructure checks to hosted API usage.

organization: NSA, CISA, FBI and international partners
title: AI Data Security: Best Practices for Securing Data Used to Train & Operate AI Systems (NSA announcement)
scope: Data provenance, integrity, protection and lifecycle changes affecting training and operational data.
limitations: The linked announcement points to the full information sheet. Local source review cannot establish provider practices or retrieval-corpus integrity.

title: Guidelines for secure AI system development
scope: Secure design, development, deployment, operation and maintenance across the AI lifecycle.
limitations: Lifecycle guidance requires implementation evidence; it does not prescribe an agent/MCP scanner or certify code.

title: JCDC AI Cybersecurity Collaboration Playbook and Fact Sheet (release notice)
scope: Incident collaboration, voluntary sharing processes and coordinated AI cybersecurity response.
limitations: Operational playbook, not a source-code scanning standard or a mandate to disclose all findings.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
scope: Risk ownership, system context, measurement and risk treatment.
limitations: Voluntary framework, not a universal technical pass/fail checklist; project mappings select security-relevant practices.

title: AI Risk Management Framework: program status
scope: Current program and revision information for AI RMF.
limitations: A changing program page is not a released replacement for the cited AI RMF 1.0 publication.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
scope: GenAI information security, privacy, data, evaluation and human interaction risks.
limitations: Broader than agent/MCP security; selected mappings do not cover the whole profile. NIST records public release on July 26, 2024.

title: AI Risk Management Framework resources
scope: Publication context and release-date provenance for AI RMF resources and the GenAI Profile.
limitations: Reference index, not a separate control framework; link to each actual publication when interpreting its requirements.

title: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations
scope: Attacker capabilities, goals and attack classes including poisoning, privacy and prompt injection.
limitations: Taxonomy is not conformance testing. The official record has a June 3, 2025 potential-updates note; check it before relying on precise identifiers.

title: Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) Version 1.1
scope: Secure engineering, software integrity, vulnerability response and release lifecycle practices.
limitations: Referenced for engineering context; this catalog is not an exhaustive SSDF compliance crosswalk.

title: Technical Blog: Strengthening AI Agent Hijacking Evaluations
scope: Adaptive attacks, repeated attempts and scenario-specific evaluation of agent hijacking.
limitations: Research methodology does not establish production assurance or a certification; report the tested harness and attack budget.

title: ATLAS tactics, techniques, mitigations and case-study data
scope: Threat modeling, adversarial AI attack paths and security-test scenario design.
limitations: Pin a content release and commit for exact IDs. Content and schema versions differ; this scanner does not calculate an ATLAS security score.

title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026
scope: Agent goals, tool use, identity, memory, code execution, communication and cascading failures.
limitations: A prioritized risk list, not an executable benchmark. Date follows the page display; machine metadata uses the following UTC day.

title: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 2026
scope: Security risks of LLM-powered applications and their connected data and execution paths.
limitations: Do not silently transfer category numbering from the 2025 edition. Date follows the displayed page rather than next-day UTC metadata.

title: OWASP MCP Top 10
scope: MCP credentials, privilege scope, tool poisoning, supply chain, injection, audit and unapproved servers.
limitations: Roadmap still describes beta/pilot even though the page also labels the project production. Treat maturity as mixed; it is not protocol conformance or benchmark completion.

title: MCP Security Cheat Sheet
scope: Practical defenses for MCP identity, tools, data boundaries, operations and exposure.
limitations: Reconcile version-sensitive recommendations against the actual deployed MCP revision; it is secondary to normative protocol requirements.

title: AI Agent Security Cheat Sheet
scope: Agent policies, isolation, context, tools and operational security testing.
limitations: General implementation guidance requires architecture-specific interpretation and runtime evidence.

title: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling
scope: Validate and encode model output before it reaches interpreters, commands, queries or presentation sinks.
limitations: Explicit historical category; its identifier must not be described as the 2026 numbering.

title: Agent Control Standard (ACS)
scope: Runtime policy hooks and enforcement architecture for agent systems.
limitations: Included as emerging architecture context; this scanner does not implement or claim conformance to ACS.

title: GenAI Security Industry Framework Crosswalk
scope: Comparison context across AI security guidance and frameworks.
limitations: Project mappings are independently scoped. Do not infer exhaustive adoption of this third-party crosswalk.

title: Model Context Protocol specification
scope: Reference revision for client/server protocol and conditional interoperability requirements.
limitations: Record the deployed revision. Versioned web pages can receive edits; pin upstream source for formal audit evidence.

title: MCP: Authorization
scope: HTTP authorization, protected-resource discovery, audience restrictions and OAuth responsibilities.
limitations: HTTP authorization is optional in the protocol; protected applications still need suitable controls. Stdio uses a different credential model.

title: MCP: Authorization Security Considerations
scope: Token validation, PKCE, issuer binding, redirects and authorization threat defenses.
limitations: Requirements are conditional on roles and deployed protocol version; decoding a token alone does not validate it.

title: MCP: Transport overview
scope: Transport selection, request metadata and compatibility across protocol revisions.
limitations: The 2026-07-28 core differs from older session and initialize-handshake designs; do not label older code a violation without checking its advertised version.

title: MCP: Streamable HTTP transport
scope: Origin validation, HTTP request behavior, streaming and transport-specific controls.
limitations: Transport compliance does not establish downstream object authorization or safe tool behavior.

title: MCP: Tools
scope: Tool input/output schemas, identity, annotations, access controls and implementation responsibilities.
limitations: Descriptions and annotations are untrusted metadata; they do not enforce read-only behavior or least privilege.

title: MCP: Sampling
scope: Host control over model sampling requests, tool access and shared context.
limitations: Sampling permission does not automatically authorize server access to user context or downstream actions.

title: MCP: Elicitation
scope: User information requests, interaction modes, sensitive data and correlated responses.
limitations: Validate supported modes and version-specific requirements; interaction affordances alone do not prevent phishing.

title: MCP: Roots
scope: Client-advertised filesystem roots and scope information supplied to servers.
limitations: Advertised roots are not an operating-system sandbox; enforce filesystem access independently.

title: MCP Security Best Practices
scope: Confused deputy, token forwarding, discovery SSRF, local launch, URL handling and registration trust.
limitations: Companion guidance is not a production assurance result. Use this moved documentation path rather than the older specification path.

title: AgentDojo
scope: Indirect prompt injection and legitimate task utility in tool workflows.
limitations: Simulated suites and evolving API; adapt to production tools and policies. Not executed here.

title: InjecAgent
scope: Malicious tool-result scenarios for tool-integrated agents.
limitations: Fixed cases are not an adaptive attacker or production permission test. Not executed here.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB)
scope: Multiple agent scenarios and attack/defense evaluation methods.
limitations: Match harness, agent, and tools; published scores do not transfer automatically. Not executed here.

title: MCPSecBench
scope: MCP security playground and attack scenarios across protocol surfaces.
limitations: Environment/client-specific research workflows; not arbitrary-repository auditing or current-spec conformance. Not executed here.
